memory_candidates.content: A vault-backed probe script that replays a two-call comparison (varying only one field) to detect server-side behavior should mint a UNIQUE session_id per invocation, never a fixed literal. Sapience's /v1/cli/context (and likely similar endpoints) applies server-side repeat/novelty suppression keyed partly by session_id (its response's status.overnight field reports 'N repeats hidden'), so reusing a fixed session_id across repeated manual test runs accumulates suppression state that can make two calls' responses differ for a reason unrelated to the field actually under test -- a false positive. Even with a unique session_id per run, residual noise can remain (the suppression may not be purely session-scoped), so a probe comparing live server responses should document a single differing run as inconclusive-leaning in its own output, never as proof a change landed.

check-extension-docs.sh's Rule U (EXTENSION.md 60-line limit) is a HARD fail() by default (SCHEMA_CONFORMANCE_GATE_MODE=hard), not advisory -- adding even one substantive paragraph to an extension's EXTENSION.md can trip it, requiring a compression pass across unrelated existing paragraphs rather than just the new one. Check the file's line count with `wc -l` immediately after any EXTENSION.md edit, before running the full gate suite, to catch this early.
